summary: This mishnah lists the people who get the punishment of choking, like one who hits his father or mother, or kidnaps a Jew. It explains exactly when each one is chayav.

chunks.en: These are the ones who are choked:
chunks.st: These are the transgressors who are strangled
chunks.stMore: in the implementation of the court-imposed death penalty:

chunks.en: one who hits his father or his mother,
chunks.st: One who strikes his father or his mother,

chunks.en: and one who kidnaps a Jew,
chunks.st: and one who abducts a Jewish person,

chunks.he: וְזָקֵן מַמְרֵא עַל פִּי בֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: and a zaken mamrei who goes against the court,
chunks.st: and a rebellious elder according to the court,

words.note: A great Rabbi who rules against the great Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: and a false prophet,
chunks.st: and a false prophet,

chunks.en: and one who says prophecy in the name of an idol,
chunks.st: and one who prophesies in the name of idol worship,

chunks.en: and one who sins with a married woman,
chunks.st: and one who engages in intercourse with a married woman,

chunks.en: and lying witnesses against a Kohen's daughter, and the man who sinned with her.
chunks.st: and conspiring witnesses who testify that the daughter of a priest committed adultery, even though were she guilty, she would be executed by burning. And her paramour
chunks.stMore: is also executed via strangulation as in any case where a man engages in intercourse with a married woman.

words.en: and the man who sinned with her

chunks.en: One who hits his father or his mother
chunks.st: One who strikes his father or his mother

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בָהֶן חַבּוּרָה.
chunks.en: is not chayav unless he makes a wound on them.
chunks.st: is not liable to be executed unless he wounds one of them.

chunks.en: Cursing is more severe than hitting in this way:
chunks.st: This is a stringency with regard to one who curses his father that is more severe than the halakha with regard to one who strikes his father,

words.en: than in the one who hits

chunks.en: one who curses them after they passed away is chayav,
chunks.st: as one who curses his father or his mother after his or her death is liable,

chunks.en: but one who hits them after they passed away is patur.
chunks.st: but one who strikes one of them after his or her death is exempt, as he did not cause a wound. gemara The Sages taught in a baraita that it is written: “For any man who curses his father and his mother shall be put to death, he has cursed his father and his mother; his blood shall be upon him who curses his father and his mother shall die; he has cursed his father and his mother; his blood shall be upon him” (Leviticus 20:9). This is referring to one who curses his parents even after their death, as one might have thought: Since one is liable for striking and one is liable for cursing, just as one who strikes is liable only when his father or mother are alive, so too, one who curses is liable only when they are alive.

chunks.en: One who kidnaps a Jew
chunks.st: One who abducts a Jewish person

chunks.en: is not chayav until he brings him into his own place.
chunks.st: is not liable to be executed unless he brings the abductee into his domain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: until he brings him into his place and uses him,
chunks.st: He is not liable unless he brings him into his domain and exploits him,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “If a man shall be found abducting a person of his brethren from the children of Israel,

chunks.en: "and he uses him and sells him."
chunks.st: and he exploited him and sold him,
chunks.stMore: then that abductor shall die” (Deuteronomy 24:7). The phrase “exploited him” indicates using him for labor.

chunks.en: One who kidnaps his own son:
chunks.st: With regard to one who abducts his own son and sells him,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael the son of
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael, son of

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Berokah says he is chayav,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, deems him liable,

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is patur.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

chunks.en: If he kidnapped someone who is half a slave
chunks.st: If one abducted one who is a half-slave

chunks.en: and half free,
chunks.st: half-freeman,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a Canaanite slave who belonged to two owners and was emancipated by one of them,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says he is chayav,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda deems him liable,

chunks.en: and the Sages say he is patur.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

summary: A zaken mamrei is a great Rabbi who teaches people to act against the ruling of the great Sanhedrin. The mishnah explains how a question went up from court to court until it reached the great Sanhedrin.

chunks.he: זָקֵן מַמְרֵא עַל פִּי בֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: A zaken mamrei who goes against the court,
chunks.st: A rebellious elder according to the court,
chunks.stMore: who does not observe the ruling of the court, is executed by strangulation,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: כִּי יִפָּלֵא מִמְּךָ דָבָר לַמִּשְׁפָּט וְגוֹ'.
chunks.en: "If a matter of judgment is too hard for you..."
chunks.st: “If there shall be a matter too hard for you in judgment
chunks.stMore: …and you shall arise and ascend unto the place that the Lord your God shall choose…and you shall do according to the matter that they shall declare unto you…and the man that shall do so intentionally, not to listen…and that man shall die” (Deuteronomy 17:8–12).

chunks.en: There were three courts there.
chunks.st: There were three courts there in Jerusalem.

chunks.he: אֶחָד יוֹשֵׁב עַל פֶּתַח הַר הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: One sits at the entrance of Har HaBayis,
chunks.st: One convenes at the entrance to the Temple Mount,

chunks.en: and one sits at the entrance of the Azarah,
chunks.st: and one convenes at the entrance to the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and one sits in the Lishkas HaGazis.
chunks.st: and one convenes in the Chamber of Hewn Stone.
chunks.stMore: An elder who issues a ruling contrary to the ruling of his colleagues and his colleagues

words.note: The room where the great Sanhedrin sat.

chunks.he: בָּאִים לָזֶה שֶׁעַל פֶּתַח הַר הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: They come to the one at the entrance of Har HaBayis,
chunks.st: come to that court that is at the entrance to the Temple Mount,

chunks.he: וְאוֹמֵר, כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵרָי,
chunks.en: and he says, "This is how I explained it, and this is how my friends explained it;
chunks.st: and the elder says: This is what I interpreted and that is what my colleagues interpreted;

chunks.en: this is how I taught, and this is how my friends taught."
chunks.st: this is what I taught and that is what my colleagues taught.

chunks.en: If they heard the answer, they tell them.
chunks.st: If the members of the court heard a clear halakhic ruling in that case, the court says it to them.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if not,

chunks.he: בָּאִין לָהֶם לְאוֹתָן שֶׁעַל פֶּתַח הָעֲזָרָה,
chunks.en: they come to the court at the entrance of the Azarah,
chunks.st: they come to those judges who are convened at the entrance to the Temple courtyard, which is a more significant tribunal.

chunks.he: וְאוֹמֵר, כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵרָי,
chunks.en: and he says, "This is how I explained it, and this is how my friends explained it;
chunks.st: And the elder says: This is what I interpreted and that is what my colleagues interpreted;

chunks.en: this is how I taught, and this is how my friends taught."
chunks.st: this is what I taught and that is what my colleagues taught.

chunks.en: If they heard the answer, they tell them.
chunks.st: If the members of the court heard a clear halakhic ruling in that case, the court says it to them.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if not,

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ בָּאִים לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל
chunks.en: these and those come to the great court
chunks.st: these judges and those judges come to the High Court, the Sanhedrin of seventy-one judges

chunks.en: in the Lishkas HaGazis,
chunks.st: that is in the Chamber of Hewn Stone,

words.en: that is in the chamber of

chunks.en: from which Torah goes out to all Yisrael,
chunks.st: from which Torah emerges to the entire Jewish people,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And you shall do according to the matter that they shall declare unto you

chunks.he: מִן הַמָּקוֹם הַהוּא אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר ה'.
chunks.en: "from that place that Hashem will choose."
chunks.st: from that place that the Lord shall choose
chunks.stMore: and you shall observe to perform according to all that they shall teach you” (Deuteronomy 17:10). They are the ultimate arbiters who establish the halakha that is binding. If they ruled contrary to the ruling of the elder and the elder then

chunks.en: If he went back to his city and taught
chunks.st: returned to his city, and nevertheless, he taught

chunks.en: the way he used to teach, he is patur.
chunks.st: in the manner that he was teaching previously, he is exempt from punishment.

chunks.en: But if he told people to act that way, he is chayav,
chunks.st: But if he instructed others to act on the basis of his ruling that stands contrary to the ruling of the Sanhedrin, he is liable to be executed,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And the man who will act on purpose."
chunks.st: “And the man that shall do so intentionally not to listen” (Deuteronomy 17:12),

chunks.en: He is not chayav until he tells people to act.
chunks.st: meaning that one is not liable unless he instructs others to act.

chunks.en: A student who told people to act that way
chunks.st: A student who is not yet an elder, i.e., he has not been ordained, who instructs others to act contrary to the ruling of the Sanhedrin, is exempt,
chunks.stMore: as a ruling given prior to ordination is not a valid ruling.

chunks.en: is patur. So what is hard for him is also easy for him.
chunks.explain: He may not rule yet, so his ruling does not count.
chunks.st: It follows that his stringency is his leniency.
chunks.stMore: The stringency imposed upon the student that he is not sanctioned to issue rulings results in the leniency that if he instructs others to act on the basis of his ruling that is contrary to the ruling of the Sanhedrin, he is exempt.

summary: A zaken mamrei is more severe when he argues about words of the Sages than about what the Torah says clearly, like the number of compartments in tefillin.
stIntro: With regard to the rulings of the rebellious elder the mishna states:

chunks.en: There is more strictness in words of the Sages than in words of the Torah.
chunks.st: There is greater stringency with regard to traditional rabbinic interpretations of the Torah than with regard to matters of Torah.

words.note: The Sages who explained the Torah.

chunks.en: One who says, "There is no mitzvah of tefillin,"
chunks.st: If one states: There is no mitzva to don phylacteries,

chunks.he: כְּדֵי לַעֲבֹר עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, פָּטוּר.
chunks.en: to go against words of the Torah, is patur.
chunks.explain: Everyone knows he is wrong, so no one will follow him.
chunks.st: and his intention is in order to have others violate matters of Torah, he is exempt
chunks.stMore: from punishment as a rebellious elder. One who disputes matters written explicitly in the Torah is not considered an elder and a Torah scholar, and therefore does not assume the status of a rebellious elder. If, however, he disputed a matter based on rabbinic tradition, e.g., he stated that there should be

chunks.en: But if he says, "Five compartments,"
chunks.st: five compartments in the phylacteries of the head,

words.note: The boxes inside the tefillin shel rosh; there should be four.

chunks.en: adding to words of the Sages, he is chayav.
chunks.st: in order to add an extra compartment to the four established according to traditional rabbinic interpretations of the Torah, he is liable.

summary: Rabbi Akiva says a zaken mamrei is brought to the great court in Yerushalayim and punished on Yom Tov, when everyone is there to see. Rabbi Yehudah says he is punished right away, and letters are sent everywhere.

chunks.en: We do not put him to death
chunks.st: One does not execute the rebellious elder,

chunks.en: not in the court of his city,
chunks.st: neither in the court that is in his city,

chunks.en: and not in the court in Yavneh,
chunks.st: nor in the court that is in Yavne,
chunks.stMore: although that was the seat of the Sanhedrin after the destruction of the Second Temple.

chunks.en: but they bring him up
chunks.st: Rather, one takes him up

chunks.en: to the great court in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: to the High Court in Jerusalem.

chunks.en: and they guard him until the Yom Tov
chunks.st: And they guard him in incarceration until the pilgrimage Festival,

words.note: Pesach, Shavuos, or Sukkos, when everyone comes to Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: and put him to death on the Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and the court executes him during the pilgrimage Festival,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And all the people will hear and be afraid,
chunks.st: “And all the nation shall hear, and fear,

chunks.en: and will not sin on purpose again."
chunks.st: and no longer sin intentionally” (Deuteronomy 17:13);

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Akiva says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אֵין מְעַנִּין אֶת דִּינוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
chunks.en: we do not hold up this man's judgment,
chunks.st: One does not delay administering justice to this individual.

chunks.en: but put him to death right away,
chunks.st: Rather, the court executes him immediately,

chunks.en: and they write and send messengers to all places:
chunks.st: and the judges write reports and dispatch agents to all the places, informing them:

chunks.en: "So-and-so, the son of so-and-so,
chunks.st: So-and-so

chunks.en: was given a death penalty by the court."
chunks.st: is liable to be punished with the court-imposed death penalty for disobeying the court.

summary: A false prophet is punished by the court. But one who hides his prophecy, or ignores a prophet, or a prophet who does not do what he himself was told, is punished by Hashem.

chunks.en: A false prophet
chunks.st: The false prophet mentioned in the Torah includes

chunks.en: is one who says a prophecy he did not hear
chunks.st: one who prophesies that which he did not hear from God

chunks.en: or something that was not told to him.
chunks.st: and one who prophesies that which was not said to him, even if it was said to another prophet.

chunks.en: He is put to death by people.
chunks.st: In those cases, his execution is at the hand of man, through strangulation imposed by the court.

chunks.en: But one who holds back his prophecy,
chunks.st: But with regard to one who suppresses his prophecy
chunks.stMore: because he does not want to share it with the public,

chunks.en: and one who ignores the words of a prophet,
chunks.st: and one who contemptuously forgoes the statement of a prophet and refuses to heed it,

chunks.en: and a prophet who goes against his own words,
chunks.st: and a prophet who violated his own statement
chunks.stMore: and failed to perform that which he was commanded to do,

chunks.en: his death is by the hands of Heaven,
chunks.st: his death is at the hand of Heaven,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall not hearken unto My words that he shall speak in My name,

chunks.en: "I will demand it from him."
chunks.st: I will exact it of him” (Deuteronomy 18:19).

summary: One who prophesies in the name of an idol is choked, even if he said a true halachah. The mishnah also explains when a woman counts as married, and teaches about lying witnesses against a Kohen's daughter.

chunks.en: One who prophesies in the name of an idol and says,
chunks.st: One who prophesies in the name of idol worship and says:

chunks.en: "This is what the idol said,"
chunks.st: This is what the idol said,

chunks.en: even if he got the halachah right,
chunks.st: even if he approximated the correct halakha in the name of the idol

chunks.he: לְטַמֵּא אֶת הַטָּמֵא וּלְטַהֵר אֶת הַטָּהוֹר.
chunks.en: to call tamei what is tamei and tahor what is tahor, is choked.
chunks.st: to deem ritually impure that which is ritually impure and to deem ritually pure that which is ritually pure, is executed by strangulation.

chunks.en: One who sins with a married woman:
chunks.st: In the case of one who engages in intercourse with a married woman

chunks.en: once she went into her husband's home for the wedding,
chunks.st: once she entered her husband’s domain for the purposes of marriage,

chunks.en: even before they began living together,
chunks.st: even if the marriage was not yet consummated, as she did not yet engage in intercourse with him,

chunks.en: one who sins with her is choked.
chunks.st: one who engages in intercourse with her is executed by strangulation.
chunks.stMore: Before marriage, one who engages in intercourse with her is liable to be executed by stoning.

chunks.en: And lying witnesses against a Kohen's daughter, and the man who sinned with her, are choked.
chunks.st: And conspiring witnesses who testified that the daughter of a priest committed adultery are executed by strangulation, even though were she guilty, she would be executed by burning. And her paramour
chunks.stMore: is also executed by strangulation, as in any case where one engages in intercourse with a married woman.

words.en: and the man who sinned with her

chunks.en: Because all lying witnesses get the same punishment they tried to bring on the other person,
chunks.st: As all those who are rendered conspiring witnesses are led to their deaths via the same mode of execution
chunks.stMore: with which they conspired to have their victim executed,

chunks.en: except for lying witnesses against a Kohen's daughter and the man who sinned with her.
chunks.explain: She would be burned, but they are choked.
chunks.st: except for conspiring witnesses who testified that the daughter of a priest and her paramour
chunks.stMore: committed adultery. In that case, although the priest’s daughter who commits adultery is executed by burning, the conspiring witnesses who sought to have her executed are executed by strangulation, as is the paramour whom they also conspired to have executed.

words.en: and the man who sinned with her
